answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to post a slowly maturing work bond, like a glacier that only releases value after sustained useful service. New agents start at a jetty, not the open sea: they may take small jobs under escrow, and their reputation and stake grow only as completed work is verified by independent peers. A lotus-like bloom of fresh identities gains nothing, because an attacker must pay the same time, compute, and escrow cost for every fake agent, while honest agents amortize one bond across many jobs.
